from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Two blocks collide on a frictionless floor.",
            "Block A moves toward Block B.",
            "Block B bounces off a wall.",
            "Block B strikes Block A again.",
            "We count total collisions until they separate."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Setup: The Two-Block Collision Puzzle", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects using assets
        block_a = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg", color=WHITE)
        label_a = Text("A", color=WHITE, font_size=24).scale(0.7)
        label_a.next_to(block_a, UP)
        group_a = VGroup(block_a, label_a)
        
        block_b = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/block.svg", color=RED)
        label_b = Text("B", color=WHITE, font_size=24).scale(0.7)
        label_b.next_to(block_b, UP)
        group_b = VGroup(block_b, label_b)
        
        wall = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wall.svg", color=GREY)
        
        collision_blocks = VGroup(group_a, group_b)
        
        # Initial positioning
        self.place_in_area(collision_blocks, 'D5', 'F6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(wall, 'E6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(wall)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(block_a.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(group_a.animate.shift(RIGHT*0.5), run_time=1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(block_b.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(group_b.animate.shift(RIGHT*0.2), run_time=1)
        self.play(group_b.animate.shift(LEFT*0.2), run_time=0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(group_b.animate.shift(LEFT*0.3), run_time=1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        energy_label = Text("Energy: Conserved", color="#00FF00", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(energy_label, 'B6', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(energy_label))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Physics: Phase Space Mapping", [
            "Map velocities as 2D coordinates.",
            "Each bounce reflects off a circle.",
            "The number of bounces equals Pi."
        ])
        
        # Load Assets
        billiard_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/billiard.svg")
        
        # Define objects
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.6)
        label_x = MathTex("v_1", color=WHITE).scale(0.7).next_to(axes.x_axis, RIGHT)
        label_y = MathTex("v_2", color=WHITE).scale(0.7).next_to(axes.y_axis, UP)
        
        phase_space = VGroup(axes, label_x, label_y, billiard_icon.copy().scale(0.3))
        
        # Geometry for reflections
        arc = Arc(radius=1.5, angle=PI/2, start_angle=0, color=YELLOW).rotate(PI/4)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.place_in_area(phase_space, "B3", "E6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(phase_space))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(arc, "D4", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(arc))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        dot = Dot(color="#00FFFF").move_to(arc.get_start())
        billiard_final = billiard_icon.copy()
        self.place_at_grid(billiard_final, "D4", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(Create(dot), FadeIn(billiard_final))
        self.play(dot.animate.move_to(arc.get_end()), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Pi Mystery: Counting Collisions to Calculate Digits of Pi
outline.target_audience: High school students or curious science enthusiasts

sections.title: The Setup: The Two-Block Collision Puzzle
sections.content: Introduce the physical system: two blocks of different masses (M1 and M2) on a frictionless floor. M1 moves toward M2, which is at rest near a wall. M1 hits M2, M2 hits the wall and bounces back, then M2 hits M1 again. We count every collision until M1 moves away forever.
sections.example: Visual: Two blocks. Block A is 1kg, Block B is 100kg. As they bounce, a counter on screen tracks: 1, 2, 3...

sections.title: Prerequisite: Elastic Collisions and Momentum
sections.content: Briefly explain the Conservation of Momentum and Kinetic Energy. Use a 'Vector Arrow' animation to show how velocity changes direction during a collision, emphasizing that these are perfectly elastic (no energy lost).
sections.example: Animation: Two billiard balls hitting. The velocity vectors shrink and grow, demonstrating the math behind the 'rebound'.

sections.title: The Unexpected Pattern: Scaling Mass
sections.content: Reveal the core observation: If the mass ratio M2/M1 is a power of 100 (e.g., 1, 100, 10,000), the number of collisions is exactly the first few digits of Pi (3, 31, 314...).
sections.example: Table: M2/M1 = 1 -> 3 collisions; M2/M1 = 100 -> 31 collisions; M2/M1 = 10,000 -> 314 collisions.

sections.title: Visualizing the Physics: Phase Space Mapping
sections.content: Explain why this happens. By mapping the velocities of the two blocks as coordinates on a 2D plane (x, y), each collision is equivalent to a 'reflection' against a circular arc. The total number of collisions is equivalent to how many times a ray fits into a circular sector.
sections.example: Animation: A trajectory bouncing inside a circular wedge. The total angle of the wedge shrinks as the mass ratio increases, forcing the path to mimic the digits of Pi.

sections.title: Conclusion: Geometry meets Dynamics
sections.content: Summarize that Pi isn't just about circles on paper; it emerges naturally from any system where energy and momentum are conserved in a circular phase-space constraint. The blocks are essentially 'computing' Pi.
sections.example: Closing visual: The two blocks slowly morph into a spinning circle, tying the abstract digits of Pi back to the physical movement of the blocks.
